pr_body:
This patch adds checkpointing to c2c cutover, which means that if the c2c job
retries on a non terminal error (e.g. a pause or node restart), the cutover
process can resume from the progress it persisted, rather than starting all
over.

This patch also fixes two bugs in the cutoverProgressTracker:
- its `getRangeCount(remainingSpans)` helper used to always return the number
  ranges in the original span to cutover, instead of the ranges that still
needed to be cutover.
- the fractionProgressed would reset to 0 when the cutover process retried. Now
  the fraction should never decrease.

Fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/97384

Release note: None

issue_context.title: c2c: checkpoint cutover progress
issue_context.body:
If the user pauses c2c cutover or some transient error causes the cutover process to restart, during resumption, the cutover process should not re-issue revert range requests on spans that have already been successfully reverted. The server handling a request on an already reverted span will return after it conducts a full scan in the `isEmptyKeyTimeRange()` fast path.  This scan, at the pebble level, can take a non-negligible amount of time if:
1. The retained data was very interspersed with the reverted data, causing pebble to issue a lot of LSM point tombstones during the initial revert range request.
2. Pebble has not yet compacted away the cleared data.

Since we want to make the cutover as fast as possible, we might as well checkpoint revert range progress and avoid this slow down case.

Jira issue: CRDB-24667

Epic CRDB-18753
